input.command: cd /testbed/src/objects; grep -n "copy(\|material = \|geometry = " Mesh.js Line.js Points.js Sprite.js SkinnedMesh.js InstancedMesh.js

cd /testbed/src/objects; sed -i 's/^\t\tthis\.material = source\.material;$/\t\tthis.material = Array.isArray( source.material ) ? source.material.slice() : source.material;/' Mesh.js Line.js Points.js; grep -n "this.material = " Mesh.js Line.js Points.js

content.text:
When you clone or copy a `Mesh`, `Line` or `Points` that uses an array of materials, the clone now gets its own copy of the array. The materials inside it are still shared, as the issue asks. I haven't run any tests.

The change is one line in each `copy()` method, in `src/objects/Mesh.js`, `Line.js` and `Points.js`:

```js
this.material = Array.isArray( source.material ) ? source.material.slice() : source.material;
```

`clone()` goes through `copy()`, so it picks this up too. Objects with a single material work exactly as before. I didn't change `Sprite`, because it uses one material, never an array.
